newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel mutual funds post massive inflow in July.
newsitem.headline: Israel mutual funds post massive inflow in July.

text.p: Israeli mutual funds posted a an inflow of 1.26 billion shekels ($355.5 million) in July, signalling a return of the public to the capital markets, Meitav Investments and Securities said on Wednesday.
Zvi Stepak, managing director of Meitav, said that because of lower interest rates the public has been shifting money from savings accounts to the capital markets via mutual funds.
The Treasury said on Wednesday that since the beginning of the year the public has withdrawn 1.2 billion shekels from savings accounts.
The massive inflow in July follows an inflow of 1.2 billion shekels in June. "In the past two months these funds had an inflow of (about) 2.5 billion shekels," Meitav said in a report.
Half of July's capital inflow -- about 594 million shekels -- was to money funds, Meitav said.
In July total assets of the mutual funds rose from about 18.40 billion shekels at the end of June to 20.59 billion shekels at the end of July.
Meitav said the rise in assets was due to the inflow of money and to the positive returns of these funds in July.
